findings_addressed.oracle: Two independent assertions: (1) getattr(reg, '_credential_loader') is concrete_loader - direct attribute inspection proves the DI argument was stored, not discarded. (2) ProviderName.ANTHROPIC in concrete_loader.calls - the _StaticCredentialLoader call log proves the registry actually invoked the loader when connect_provider() was called without explicit credentials. (3) provider.is_connected - proves the credentials fetched by the loader were successfully used to complete the connection.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/providers/registry.py ProviderRegistry.__init__, change `self._credential_loader = credential_loader` to `self._credential_loader = None` — the assert stored_loader is concrete_loader assertion will fail immediately.

notes: Removed the unused CredentialLoaderProtocol import (the old test used it for a type annotation on the local variable; the hardened test uses the concrete _StaticCredentialLoader type directly). The test is now fully falsifiable: asserting the stored loader identity catches silent discard of the DI argument, and asserting the call log exercises the end-to-end path from connect_provider through the loader to connect().
